papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Robust Real-World Image Super-Resolution against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: Recently deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success in real-world image super-resolution (SR). However, adversarial image samples with quasi-imperceptible noises could threaten deep learning SR models. In this paper, we propose a robust deep learning framework for real-world SR that randomly erases potential adversarial noises in the frequency domain of input images or features. The rationale is that on the SR task clean images or features have a different pattern from the attacked ones in the frequency domain. Observing that existing adversarial attacks usually add high-frequency noises to input images, we introduce a novel random frequency mask module that blocks out high-frequency components possibly containing the harmful perturbations in a stochastic manner. Since the frequency masking may not only destroys the adversarial perturbations but also affects the sharp details in a clean image, we further develop an adversarial sample classifier based on the frequency domain of images to determine if applying the proposed mask module. Based on the above ideas, we devise a novel real-world image SR framework that combines the proposed frequency mask modules and the proposed adversarial classifier with an existing super-resolution backbone network. Experiments show that our proposed method is more insensitive to adversarial attacks and presents more stable SR results than existing models and defenses.

literature_themes.theme: Robustness in Deep Learning Against Adversarial Attacks
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models in the face of adversarial attacks, specifically in recommendation systems and image super-resolution tasks. The first paper presents a dual-defense framework that combines active and passive defenses to mitigate data poisoning in recommendation systems, while the second paper introduces a frequency domain approach to counter adversarial noise in image super-resolution, demonstrating improved model performance and security.
literature_themes.limitations: Both papers highlight the challenge of balancing model robustness with performance. The first paper does not address the potential computational overhead of the dual-defense framework, and the second paper may struggle with the trade-off between removing adversarial noise and preserving image details. Additionally, the effectiveness of these methods in diverse real-world scenarios remains to be fully validated.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies a significant research gap in developing comprehensive defense mechanisms against various forms of adversarial attacks across different domains. It underscores the need for further exploration of hybrid defense strategies and their applicability in real-world settings, providing a foundation for future studies aimed at enhancing the resilience of deep learning systems.

summary: The retrieved literature emphasizes the development of robust AI systems to counter data poisoning and adversarial attacks, focusing on deep learning applications in recommendation systems and image super-resolution. Key contributions include a dual-defense framework that integrates active and passive defenses to enhance model integrity in recommendation systems, and a frequency domain approach that improves resilience against adversarial noise in image processing. However, both studies reveal limitations regarding computational overhead and the challenge of maintaining performance while ensuring robustness, highlighting a critical gap in adaptive defense strategies for evolving attack landscapes.
scholarly_positioning: Prior approaches to enhancing robustness in AI systems, particularly in recommendation systems and image super-resolution, have introduced innovative frameworks such as dual-defense mechanisms and frequency domain strategies. However, these methods often grapple with unresolved tensions, including the trade-off between model performance and robustness, as well as the computational overhead associated with complex defense systems. Existing work remains insufficient as it fails to address the adaptability of these defenses in the face of evolving adversarial tactics and dynamic environments. The proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by exploring hybrid defense strategies that not only enhance resilience against diverse adversarial attacks but also maintain operational efficiency and model integrity across various real-world applications.
research_scope: This empirical study will focus on enhancing the robustness of deep learning models specifically in recommendation systems and image super-resolution tasks, targeting the challenges posed by data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The research will evaluate a hybrid defense strategy that integrates a dual-defense framework with adaptive filtering techniques over a 12-month evaluation period. The primary outcomes will include the success rates of adversarial attacks and the quality of recommendations or image outputs, while secondary outcomes will assess computational efficiency and model performance metrics. A control group will consist of traditional defense mechanisms currently employed in these domains to establish a baseline for comparison.

technical_feasibility: The study requires access to open-source deep learning models for the dual-defense framework and adaptive filtering techniques, as well as labeled datasets for training and evaluation. It will also need GPU resources for computational efficiency during experiments. Since the study involves evaluating user trust in the recommendation systems, it will require a human-subject design and appropriate trust calibration measures. Missing resources include specific user feedback mechanisms and potential ethics approval for human participants. A feasible adjustment would be to focus on simulated user interactions or synthetic datasets to bypass the need for direct human involvement while still assessing trust calibration.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of dual-defense frameworks in enhancing robustness against data poisoning in recommendation systems; however, they treat the adaptability of these defenses to evolving attack strategies as secondary, leaving unclear whether dynamic environments affect the performance of these frameworks. This matters practically because the landscape of adversarial attacks is constantly changing, necessitating defenses that can evolve accordingly; therefore, this study investigates the integration of adaptive filtering techniques with existing dual-defense frameworks to enhance resilience in real-world applications.
question: How does the integration of adaptive filtering techniques with a dual-defense framework enhance the robustness of deep learning models in recommendation systems against evolving data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to traditional defense mechanisms?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates how the integration of adaptive filtering techniques (independent variable) with a dual-defense framework influences the robustness of deep learning models (dependent variable) in recommendation systems against evolving data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The adaptive filtering techniques serve as a mediator by dynamically adjusting model responses based on incoming data characteristics, enhancing system resilience. The dual-defense framework acts as a moderator, potentially amplifying the effects of adaptive filtering on robustness. System-level outcomes, such as unsafe response rate and refusal accuracy, are mediated by technical mechanisms like representation features and filters, while user-level outcomes, including trust and satisfaction, are mediated by psychological mechanisms such as perceived transparency. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of adaptive filtering in real-time adjustments and the interaction effects between dual-defense strategies and adaptive mechanisms in varying attack scenarios.
hypothesis: The integration of adaptive filtering techniques (independent variable) with a dual-defense framework will result in significantly higher robustness (primary dependent variable) of deep learning models in recommendation systems against evolving data poisoning and adversarial attacks compared to traditional defense mechanisms (comparison/control), with adaptive filtering enhancing the effectiveness of the dual-defense framework as a mediator.

Causal Pathway:
The integration of adaptive filtering techniques (IV) is hypothesized to enhance the robustness of deep learning models (DV) through the dual-defense framework (moderator), which may amplify the effectiveness of the adaptive filtering. The unsafe response rate (output-level) will be assessed to evaluate the system's resilience against attacks, while trust calibration (user-level) will provide insights into user perception.

Likely Confounds:
Potential confounding variables include the variability in attack strategies, differences in dataset quality, and the inherent complexity of deep learning models that may affect robustness independently of the proposed interventions.

Claim Boundaries:
The study claims that the integration of adaptive filtering techniques will lead to improved robustness compared to traditional methods, but it cannot conclude causality without controlling for all confounding variables. Additionally, the results may not generalize beyond the specific contexts of recommendation systems and image super-resolution tasks. The study does not imply that adaptive filtering alone is sufficient for robustness without the dual-defense framework's support.
methodology: This study will employ an experimental design to evaluate the effectiveness of a hybrid defense strategy integrating adaptive filtering techniques with a dual-defense framework in enhancing the robustness of deep learning models in recommendation systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks. The research will utilize labeled datasets for training and evaluation, with a control group consisting of traditional defense mechanisms to establish baseline performance metrics. Key operationalized variables include the success rates of adversarial attacks, unsafe response rates, and trust calibration measures, which will be assessed through algorithm performance metrics and user surveys. Statistical analyses will be conducted to compare the robustness of the proposed hybrid approach against the control group, controlling for confounding variables such as dataset quality and attack variability. To ensure reproducibility, the study will utilize open-source models and publicly available datasets, while the scope will be limited to recommendation systems and image super-resolution tasks to maintain focus on the research question.

proposal: This research proposal aims to enhance the robustness of deep learning models in recommendation systems and image super-resolution tasks against data poisoning and adversarial attacks by integrating adaptive filtering techniques with a dual-defense framework. Robust AI systems are defined as those maintaining performance in the presence of adversarial inputs, while data poisoning refers to malicious data injected into training sets. The study will utilize open-source deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks for image processing and collaborative filtering algorithms for recommendation systems, and labeled datasets, requiring GPU resources for computational efficiency. Scholarly positioning highlights the limitations of existing dual-defense frameworks in adapting to evolving attack strategies, revealing a critical gap in the literature regarding the need for dynamic defenses that can adjust to new attack vectors. The research question focuses on how the integration of adaptive filtering techniques enhances robustness compared to traditional defenses, specifically examining the effectiveness of these techniques in real-time adjustments to model responses. The theoretical mechanism posits that adaptive filtering serves as a mediator, dynamically adjusting model responses, while the dual-defense framework acts as a moderator, amplifying robustness. The falsifiable hypothesis states that the proposed hybrid approach will demonstrate significantly higher robustness than traditional methods, measured by success rates of adversarial attacks and unsafe response rates. Construct operationalization includes metrics for success rates of adversarial attacks (output-level), unsafe response rates (output-level), and trust calibration (user-level), with controls established through traditional defense mechanisms. The methodology employs experimental design and performance benchmarking to assess the effectiveness of the hybrid strategy, utilizing statistical analyses to ensure validity and reproducibility. Expected contributions include theoretical insights into adaptive filtering's role in robustness, technical advancements in hybrid defense strategies, empirical data on performance metrics, and practical guidelines for real-world applications. Key limitations include potential confounding variables such as variability in attack strategies and dataset quality, which will be controlled through sensitivity analyses and robust statistical methods.
